title: Squeaky's Lost Day
markdown:
The late afternoon sun painted soft, golden patterns on Rowan's warm wooden floor. Her little cottage, snugged down in the gentle hills, always smelled of sweet pine and soft, damp earth after a quiet rain. Rowan was a kind witch. Her magic helped tiny seeds open and warmed cold toes, not loud, booming spells. Today, she was putting little dewdrop charms in a neat line on her windowsill. She really loved her quiet life. Rowan believed the best magic was simply being kind.

Then, a tiny, worried squeak came from the windowsill. Rowan looked closer. A very, very small mouse shivered there. Its fur was soft and grey, like a little cloud. Its tiny whiskers twitched. The little mouse looked lost, far from its cozy home. Rowan’s heart felt a little flutter. She knew she had to help this little creature. This was the start of her gentle evening journey.

Rowan softly opened the window. A whisper of sweet evening air came in. "Hello, little one," she whispered, her voice soft as falling leaves. "Are you lost, little friend?" The mouse squeaked again. It sounded like a big, clear "Yes!" Rowan gently scooped the mouse into her warm hands. It felt so light and warm. "I'll call you Squeaky," she smiled. Squeaky twitched his little nose. "Now, where is your home, little Squeaky? We must find it before the moon wakes up."

But Squeaky, though sweet, was also a little bit stubborn sometimes. He would scamper ahead, then stop suddenly, sniffing the air. Rowan tried to follow a faint, tiny scent, like dandelion fluff on a soft breeze. But the winding paths through the tall, whispering pines were confusing. The trees seemed to lean in, their soft needles murmuring secrets. Rowan wasn't sure if they were helping or just sharing playful gossip.

As they walked along, a funny man came from behind a big, mossy rock. It was Wizard Fitzwilliam. His long white beard nearly swept the ground. "Hello, Rowan!" he boomed, his voice warm like warm apple drink on a cold day. "Out for a walk with a new friend?" Rowan explained about Squeaky. Wizard Fitzwilliam nodded. "A lost pet! Oh dear. I have just the thing!" He rummaged in a pocket. Maps tumbled out! Maps of stars, maps of underground rivers, maps of places only in dreams. "Where was your friend going?" he murmured, looking at a map drawn on a leaf. Rowan pointed. "Somewhere near here? He knows the way, but then he stops." Wizard Fitzwilliam tapped a map. "Ah, yes! Follow this wiggly line, past the giggling brook and under the sleeping owl tree. We'll be there fast!" He gave Rowan a map that looked like a happy dragon. Rowan tried to follow his directions, but they led them in funny circles. The lantern Rowan carried glowed softly, casting playful shadows that danced like happy fireflies.

The moon was just peeking over the mountain tops, painting the sky with soft purple and pink. Rowan looked around. The tall pines seemed taller now. The path was harder to see. Squeaky snuggled in her pocket, a tiny ball of warmth. Rowan felt a small, shy worry. "Oh dear," she whispered. "We've wandered a little far." The lantern's soft light felt like a small pool in the growing, peaceful dimness.

The path grew more tangled with leafy bushes. The whispering pines murmured their secrets a little louder. Their rustling needles sounded like hushed, playful whispers. Rowan couldn't see any familiar places. She sat down on a soft, mossy spot. She put Squeaky gently beside her on fallen leaves. He looked up at her with his bright, black eyes, so trusting and sweet. Rowan felt a little pang of sadness. She hadn't brought Squeaky home tonight, like she promised. The lantern’s light seemed to dim a little, like her quiet, tender care.

Rowan sighed softly, a gentle sound. "It seems we won't find your cozy home tonight, little Squeaky," she whispered, her voice full of comfort. She took a soft, woven blanket from her bag and wrapped it around them both, like a warm hug. "But you'll be safe and warm with me. We will try our very best to find your home in the morning, when the sun is high and the path is clear." She gave Squeaky a smooth, warm pebble from her pocket. He nibbled it gently. Then he curled up against her hand, a tiny ball of happy, sleepy warmth. She realized, in that quiet moment, that sometimes, even with the kindest plans, things just take their own gentle time. And being truly kind meant offering comfort and safety, even when plans don't work out perfectly.

The next morning, as the sun warmed the hills, Rowan woke to a soft, happy squeak. Squeaky was pointing his tiny nose towards some mossy rocks nearby. And there, nestled between the rocks, was a tiny, perfect mouse-sized door with a green leaf for a roof! Rowan gasped with delight. "Squeaky! Your home! It was so close all along!" Just then, Wizard Fitzwilliam ambled by, looking pleased as he sorted his scrolls. "Ah, Rowan! I believe I've finally sorted my maps!" he declared, his eyes twinkling. "And look," he said, pointing his walking stick. "Your friend's home was right here all along! My map of 'Hidden Homes of the Forest' was tucked very neatly under my map of 'Where the Cloud Sheep Graze'," he chuckled, a dry, witty sound. It seemed the wizard’s muddled maps had led them on a surprising journey, but not entirely the wrong one.

Rowan gently placed Squeaky at his little door. He squeaked a happy, grateful goodbye and scampered inside his cozy home. Rowan watched him go, a warm, happy feeling spreading through her like sunshine. Kindness, she knew, was the most magical power of all. She waved goodbye to Wizard Fitzwilliam. He was already talking to a busy beetle about the best path to the Whispering Waterfall. As Rowan turned to walk back to her own cozy cottage, the hills felt wonderfully peaceful and bright. She looked up at the clear blue sky, dreaming of the day’s gentle, happy adventures. And soon, she knew, she would be tucked into her own warm bed, ready for the sweetest, most peaceful dreams.
characters: Rowan the young witch, a mouse
